doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Opening and the Hamilton concert
summary: Rowe opens part 2 and recalls the earlier session about 23 years before. He mentions the Hamilton concert and asks what Pizzarelli says to pianist Isaiah Thompson on stage.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and this is a long-delayed Part 2 interview with John Pizzarelli. Do you know that it was twenty — I can’t do the math —

No it was more like, I think it was 2000. And we were in New York and we had a wonderful session and I just would like to say, and I hope you agree with me that both you and I haven’t aged a day, don’t you think?
I don’t know — we look great.

Well that’s a good place to start. I had the pleasure with about 200 plus other people of having you to Hamilton a couple of weeks ago and it was a marvelous concert. There was a couple of things I wanted to ask you about it. You have a terrific piano player with Isaiah Thompson, and there was a few moments throughout the night, he was sitting to your left, and you would lean over while you were playing and say something to him. And the person that was sitting next to me and I were sort of wondering, well what are they talking about? Going out for pizza afterwards or something? Can you give us an inside story of what those little exchanges are for?
